claims.text: Random mixing of the six noble metals creates a distribution of distinct active sites.
The distinct active sites possess a distribution of modulated d-band centers.
The electronic structure optimally balances adsorption and desorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
This tuned electronic structure is essential for high ethanol-oxidation activity and selectivity.
Fresh nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts have a homogeneous random-alloy structure.
The as-prepared PtPdRhRuIrOs surface has a characteristic distribution of noble-metal oxidation states.
A mild anodic electrochemical pretreatment in oxygenated electrolyte will partially oxidize the catalyst surface and alter its surface oxidation-state distribution.
Local atomic configuration in the disordered solid solution governs d-band-center shifts at individual metal sites.
Random mixing of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os induces interatomic charge redistribution.
Charge redistribution produces a spread of d-band centers across the PtPdRhRuIrOs surface.
The spread of d-band centers tunes adsorption energies of reaction intermediates.
Oxidative pretreatment will disturb the alloy's synergistic electronic interactions by shifting surface oxidation states.
The pretreatment-induced electronic disturbance will make adsorption and desorption energetics less optimal and impede the catalytic cycle.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the pre-oxidized catalyst will have lower ethanol-oxidation current density.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the pre-oxidized catalyst will have an onset-potential shift toward higher overpotential.
The as-prepared PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has previously reported high ethanol-oxidation activity and selectivity.
The proposed mechanism should apply under typical ethanol-oxidation pH and temperature ranges.
Extreme oxidation or reduction may significantly alter the catalyst structure and invalidate the mechanism.
